source.title: Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
source.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) -- Best Paper

confidence_rationale: Foundational, high-quality evidence for the UNDERLYING premise of MECH-472 -- that low training-context error carries essentially no information about acquisition, because a sufficiently expressive learner can drive training error to zero on random labels it cannot possibly have 'understood'. That is the strongest possible demonstration that in-context success and genuine competence are dissociable. Mapping fidelity is discounted because the setting is supervised image classification with i.i.d. train/test SAMPLES, not an agent generalising across CONTEXTS; MECH-472's held-out CONTEXT notion is stronger than a held-out sample split, so the paper supports the principle but not the specific held-out-context construct.
failure_signatures: A network can reach zero training error on data with randomly permuted labels, proving that perfect fit to the training distribution is achievable with no generalisable structure whatsoever -- so training-context performance cannot certify acquisition.

Explicit regularisation is neither necessary nor sufficient to control the generalisation gap, so one cannot infer 'this competence generalises' from the presence of a regulariser or a low training loss.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Deep networks can perfectly fit training data with random labels or random pixels, achieving zero training error while generalising at chance; their effective capacity is enough to memorise the entire dataset, and traditional complexity measures fail to explain their generalisation.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-472 assumes that success measured on the contexts that produced a competence update is uninformative about whether real skill was acquired. Zhang et al. give the sharpest form of that assumption: a learner can drive in-context error to zero purely by memorising, with zero transfer -- hence the necessity of evaluating on data the competence was not fit to.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The demonstration is in supervised classification with held-out SAMPLES from the same distribution, not an agent evaluated on held-out CONTEXTS/tasks. MECH-472's construct is stronger (a context that did not generate the competence, not just an unseen i.i.d. point), so this paper supports the general dissociation of fit-vs-acquisition but does not itself instantiate held-out-context evaluation.
mapping.source_context: Supervised deep learning; CIFAR-10 and ImageNet image classification with Inception/AlexNet/MLP architectures; no agent, no reward, no sequential decision-making.

confidence_components.notes: Weighted toward mapping_fidelity for this architectural/methodological claim: the finding is rock-solid but one abstraction level up from REE's competence-promotion setting. Transfer risk reflects the supervised->agentic and sample->context jumps.
